headline: Corn steadies near $4.81 after Friday's WASDE hit
lead: Corn is at $4.81 overnight, up 1¼¢ from Friday's $4.79¾ settle, a small bounce after Friday's near 4% drop on USDA's yield number. Soybean meal gained 2.2% to $368.70 while beans slipped to $12.83. Monday's quiet bounce doesn't undo Friday's loss on unpriced corn.
teaser: Corn holds steady after Friday's WASDE drop; meal leads the soy complex higher.

one_number.unit: daily rate to charter a supertanker Gulf to China
one_number.context: Supertanker rates pulled back from an all-time high this month as the Iran-Hormuz premium cools, even with two more tankers hit over the weekend.

sections.title: Corn finds its feet after WASDE
sections.body:
- Corn is at **$4.81** overnight, up 1¼¢, a day after Friday's near 4% drop on USDA's yield number.
- Soybeans slipped 9¼¢ to $12.83 even with a record crop already priced in from Friday.
- Soybean meal gained 2.2% to $368.70, the biggest move in the grain complex today.
sections.so_what: Meal is doing the work in soy, not beans themselves.

sections.title: Cattle and feeders keep climbing
sections.body:
- Live cattle are at **$224.98** overnight, up 1.4% from Friday's $221.88 settle.
- Feeders are up 1.7% to $343.85, extending last week's strength with no Cattle on Feed report behind it.
- The cattle herd sits at a 75-year low, and that scarcity keeps showing up in both contracts.
sections.so_what: Tight supply, not a report, is still driving the cattle bid.

sections.title: Crude firms as tankers take more hits
sections.body:
- WTI crude is at **$92.52** overnight, up 0.7%, after two more tankers were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend.
- That's part of the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a re-escalation since July that has cooled and flared more than once since spring.
sections.so_what: Diesel policy news matters more to farmers right now than another tanker headline.

outside_the_pit.title: HPAI confirmed in two Washington dairy herds
outside_the_pit.body: These are the state's first avian flu detections in dairy cattle, adding to a small but steady trickle of cases nationally this year.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress, delayed a day for Columbus Day. Harvest pace matters more than usual after USDA raised the corn yield on Friday.
Export sales. Strong soybean numbers would help offset Friday's record-crop weight on the board.
Corn back under $4.75 would say Friday's WASDE loss still has room to run.

source_summary: CME/CBOT overnight quotes as of 5:45 a.m. CT; USDA WASDE; oilprice.com; thefencepost.com; feedstuffs.com; agweb.com

lines: Corn harvest price so far: $4.98 vs $4.62 projected (+7.8%), 7 of 22 trading days in.
Soybeans harvest price so far: $12.89 vs $11.09 projected (+16.2%), 7 of 22 trading days in.
harvest_clock.note: Average of the daily CBOT settles through Oct 9, figured the way USDA RMA does. Window and projected price: USDA RMA, as of Oct 11. Oct 1-31 window, most states.
